plain_description.what: No calls. A positive control for the significance check: inside math, physics and economics, the questions were split two ways by known source (original MMLU questions vs added sources), resized to the earlier test's sizes, and run through the same certificate 30 times.
plain_description.why: An earlier test certified 0 of 60 splits. This one asks whether that is because the check is too weak to detect a simple two-way split inside one subject.
plain_description.information: If the known split were certified, the check would be shown sensitive enough and the earlier 0 of 60 would reflect weak structure. If not, the check might simply be blind at this size. Result: done. The known split was certified on none of the 30 runs; its separation was below every random baseline. This is read as a failed positive control: it cannot tell 'the check is not sensitive enough' apart from 'source families are only weakly separated'. The earlier conclusions are unchanged.
